userStories.title: VCS connection writes are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Couple VCS connection create, update, delete and webhook-secret rotation to a safe AuditEntry in each write's transaction.

**Motivation** — Every human route and every fleet writer now leaves an entry, but a ticket imported from a GitHub issue, a PR merge that moves a ticket to `VERIFY_FIX`, a VCS connection whose token was replaced and a ticket a CI pipeline opened leave none.

**Approach** — The command layer writes `AuditEntry` in the domain write's transaction. The package's `AuditInterceptor` and `@Audit` decorator are not used.

A connection summary never carries a token, a secret or an author list. Create records the provider, the repo and the sync mode. Update records the changed field names through `fieldsSummary`, never values: it is called on `updateData` with `encryptedToken` renamed `token`, so the names are `token`, `syncMode`, `allowedAuthors`, `pollingIntervalMs` and `webhookSecret` (present only when the update generated a secret). Rotation records a fixed text. An issue import names the issue number only, never its title or body. A PR-state entry names the states only, never the PR URL, title or merge author.

`apps/api/src/vcs/vcs-connection.service.ts` — injects AuditRecorder as the last constructor parameter and runs create's, update's, delete's and rotateWebhookSecret's repository write inside audit.audited with the contract's entry; validation, the 409 and 404 paths, the no-change return and the polling refresh are unchanged.

Contract:
| Write | Key | resourceType | resourceId | projectId | summary |
| VCS connection created | `vcs.connection.create` | `vcs-connection` | connection id | the project | `<provider> <owner>/<name>, sync <mode>` (e.g. `github acme/app, sync webhook`) |
| VCS connection updated | `vcs.connection.update` | `vcs-connection` | connection id | the project | `fieldsSummary` of `updateData` with `encryptedToken` renamed `token` (e.g. `fields: syncMode, token`) |
| VCS connection deleted | `vcs.connection.delete` | `vcs-connection` | connection id | the project | `deleted <provider> <owner>/<name>` |
| webhook secret rotated | `vcs.webhook-secret.rotate` | `vcs-connection` | connection id | the project | `webhook secret rotated` |

The connection routes and the three manual sync routes record as the request's actor, origin `rest`. No entry in this feature sets `onBehalfOf`. `projectId` is the row's project. A failed record rolls back its mutation; create must not schedule polling on failure. Leave scheduler refresh/unschedule after successful commit. An empty patch returns the stored connection with no write or entry.

Preserve existing assertions while adding `{ provide: AuditRecorder, useValue: mockAuditRecorder }` to vcs-connection.service.spec.ts testing modules in src and test/integration/vcs, and pass mockAuditRecorder last to direct constructors in vcs-connection.webhook-secret.spec.ts and vcs-connection.gitlab.spec.ts. The global audit module already supplies the production dependency. Create the named integration spec using the shared real-AppModule fixture and failure-spy protocol in analysis.

**Scope** — In: four connection mutation boundaries, safe summaries, rollback behavior and affected constructor consumers. Out: US-002 issue imports/helper types; US-003 PR states; US-004 merges; US-005 derived links/effects; US-006 CI/replay attribution. `POST /projects/:slug/vcs/test` (`vcs.connection.test`) writes no row and records nothing.

**Interface** — Existing recorder contract (read-only): `AuditRecorder.record(input)` and `AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf)` (`entriesOf` may return `[]`), `AuditRecordInput { key; resourceType; resourceId; projectId?; summary? }`. `fieldsSummary(patch)` — sorted field names of the defined values, `undefined` for none. Public connection methods/DTOs/routes do not change.

userStories.title: VCS issue imports are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Audit each imported issue ticket inside its number-allocation attempt using the caller's entry-point key and add the shared VCS audit contract.

**Motivation** — Those are writes an outside system caused, and the Audit log is the only place that would show which integration made them and when.

**Approach** — An entry names the entry point, not the shared helper. `syncIssue` and the PR-state writes are shared by a route, the poller and the webhook intake. The caller passes the key: `vcs.sync.issue` (one-issue route), `vcs.sync.all` (full-sync route), `vcs.sync.pr` (PR-sync route), `system.vcs.poll-issues` (the poller, issues and PR states alike) or `system.vcs.webhook-intake` (the webhook). The inventory rows are per entry point, so the walker in audit-coverage can match them.

Ticket creation records inside the ticket-number retry. `createTicketFromIssue` and `PrismaCiWebhookRepository.createTicket` run in `runWithTicketNumberRetry`, which starts a fresh transaction per attempt and refuses to retry inside an outer one (`ticket-number-retry.ts:38`). Wrapping them in `audited` would turn every number conflict into a 409. Both gain an optional last parameter `onCreated: (ticket) => Promise<void>`, run inside the attempt's transaction after the insert, and the services pass a callback that calls `record`. This is the `MembershipService.createBinding(…, onWritten)` pattern from audit-core.

The issues webhook keeps swallowing its errors. `handleIssueOpened` catches every error and answers 200 `success: false` (`vcs-webhook.service.ts:250`), so the controller does not forget the delivery id and GitHub's redelivery is refused as a replay. A rejected `record` therefore loses that import, as any database error does today. Changing the intake's error contract is out of scope; AC13 of US-002 pins the behaviour so the coverage or delivery feature can revisit it.

`apps/api/src/vcs/vcs-sync.service.ts` — injects AuditRecorder right after vcsRepo (before the optional vcsConfig); syncIssue gains the required auditKey parameter and passes createTicketFromIssue an onCreated callback that records it on the new ticket; fullSync passes 'vcs.sync.all'; dedup and author filtering are unchanged.
`apps/api/src/vcs/domain/vcs.repository.ts` — createTicketFromIssue gains the optional last onCreated parameter.
`apps/api/src/vcs/prisma-vcs.repository.ts` — createTicketFromIssue awaits onCreated with the inserted ticket inside the retry attempt's transaction, after ticket.create; number allocation and the retry are unchanged.
`apps/api/src/vcs/vcs.controller.ts` — the one-issue sync route passes 'vcs.sync.issue' to syncIssue; responses are unchanged.
`apps/api/src/vcs/vcs-polling.service.ts` — poll passes 'system.vcs.poll-issues' to syncIssue; scheduling, the cursor and the sync log are unchanged.
`apps/api/src/vcs/vcs-webhook.service.ts` — handleIssueOpened passes 'system.vcs.webhook-intake' to syncIssue; its result mapping is unchanged.

Contract: issue imported | the caller's `VcsIssueAuditKey` | `resourceType` `ticket` | `resourceId` the new ticket's id | `projectId` the project | `summary` `imported issue #<n>`. `<n>` is the VCS issue number. An issue import names the issue number only, never its title or body. The connection routes and the three manual sync routes record as the request's actor, origin `rest`. The poller and the webhook intake record as `SYSTEM/vcs` (`runAsSystemWriter` in `VcsPollingService.tick` and `VcsWebhookService.handleWebhook`, unchanged), origin `system`. No entry in this feature sets `onBehalfOf`.

Dedup includes soft-deleted externalVcsId matches and records nothing. record failure is not a number conflict and is not retried. One-issue HTTP propagates an error; fullSync counts the issue skipped and lists its error; the poller's single try stops at that issue, logs, keeps its cursor and skips PR sync, leaving later issues for a later tick; issue webhook preserves its 200 success:false/replay behavior. Update all required-key call sites and repository callback assertions without weakening existing tests. Add mockAuditRecorder providers to the affected src/integration sync and polling specs listed in analysis; direct VcsSyncService constructors receive it second. Add fake-timer forwarding assertion in vcs-polling.tick.spec.ts and callback-to-record assertion in vcs-sync.service.spec.ts.

**Scope** — In: issue imports at four entry points, repository callback seam, shared vcs-audit.ts types/helper and regression consumers. Out: US-001 connection mutations; US-003 PR-state wiring consumes this helper afterward; US-004 merge ownership; US-005 extractor upsert return changes; US-006 implements the separate CI callback and replay attribution. The runtime coverage guard and the walker test over write surfaces are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-coverage`). The Bookkeeping table is its input. Recording the update branches of `upsertTicketLink` and `upsertFleetPrLink`, a same-state webhook PR write, the poller's `VcsSyncLog` rows and cursor, the replay rows and a push's `code_commit` outbox rows is out of scope (the Bookkeeping table). Changing the ticket-number allocation, `runWithTicketNumberRetry`, the replay guard's rules, the dedup of pushes or any route's status codes, response bodies or `@Requires` keys is out of scope; `openapi.json` does not change.

**Interface** — Create `src/vcs/vcs-audit.ts` with:
```typescript
/** The key an issue import records: the entry point that ran syncIssue. */
export type VcsIssueAuditKey = 'vcs.sync.issue' | 'vcs.sync.all' | 'system.vcs.poll-issues' | 'system.vcs.webhook-intake';

/** The key a PR-state write records: the entry point that saw the state. */
export type VcsPrStateAuditKey = 'vcs.sync.pr' | 'system.vcs.poll-issues' | 'system.vcs.webhook-intake';

/** `pr <before> -> <after>`; `before` is `none` for a link with no stored state. */
export function prStateSummary(before: string | null, after: string): string;
```
`VcsSyncService.syncIssue(project, issue, syncMode, repo)` → `syncIssue(project, issue, syncMode, repo, auditKey: VcsIssueAuditKey)`.
`IVcsRepository.createTicketFromIssue(project, issue, externalVcsId)` gains an optional last `onCreated: (ticket: { id: string; number: number }) => Promise<void>`. Preserve CreateTicketFromIssueResult including its title. Implement the helper body, not just a declaration.

userStories.title: VCS PR-state writes are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Audit non-merge PR-state mutations from manual sync, polling and the five webhook handlers without recording same-state or unsuccessful writes.

**Motivation** — Those are writes an outside system caused, and the Audit log is the only place that would show which integration made them and when.

**Approach** — An entry names the entry point, not the shared helper. `syncIssue` and the PR-state writes are shared by a route, the poller and the webhook intake. The caller passes the key: `vcs.sync.issue` (one-issue route), `vcs.sync.all` (full-sync route), `vcs.sync.pr` (PR-sync route), `system.vcs.poll-issues` (the poller, issues and PR states alike) or `system.vcs.webhook-intake` (the webhook). The inventory rows are per entry point, so the walker in audit-coverage can match them.

A webhook PR-state write records only when the stored state changes. `updateTicketLinkWithPrState` returns `'updated'` for a same-state write too (it bumps `prUpdatedAt`). The webhook records when the outcome is `'updated'` and the link's state before the write differs from the new one. The poller and the PR-sync route already write only when the state differs (`vcs-pr-sync.service.ts:93`).

The extractor's entries can land after `syncPrStatus` resolves. `syncPrStatus` starts `extractLinksFromPr` without awaiting it (`vcs-pr-sync.service.ts:111`) when the PR status has a `branchName` and the link has a ticket, so in the PR-sync route and the poller its `ticket.link.add` entries are written asynchronously, still under the caller's context. That is unchanged; tests of `syncPrStatus` stub a status without `branchName`.

The 404 close catches its own failure. In `syncPrStatus` the 404 close runs inside the per-link `catch` (`vcs-pr-sync.service.ts:131`), so a rejection there would escape the loop and abort the rest of the sync, and through the poller the whole poll. It gets its own `try`/`catch` that logs and counts the link skipped, like the main write.

`apps/api/src/vcs/vcs-pr-sync.service.ts` — injects AuditRecorder right after vcsRepo (before the optional parameters); syncPrStatus gains the required auditKey parameter and runs each non-merge prState write, including the 404 close, inside audit.audited, recording the key when the write returned 'updated', and wraps the 404 close in its own try/catch that logs and counts the link skipped; the merge branch and the link extraction are unchanged in this story.
`apps/api/src/vcs/vcs-webhook.service.ts` — injects AuditRecorder right after vcsConfig (before the two optional parameters) and runs the five non-merge PR handlers' prState write inside audit.audited, recording system.vcs.webhook-intake when it returned 'updated' and the stored state changed; outcomes and ignore reasons are unchanged.
`apps/api/src/vcs/vcs.controller.ts` — the PR sync route passes 'vcs.sync.pr' to syncPrStatus; responses are unchanged.
`apps/api/src/vcs/vcs-polling.service.ts` — poll passes 'system.vcs.poll-issues' to syncPrStatus.

Contract: PR state changed (not merged) | the caller's `VcsPrStateAuditKey` | `resourceType` `ticket-link` | `resourceId` link id | `projectId` the project | `summary` `prStateSummary(<before>, <after>)` (e.g. `pr open -> closed`). A PR-state entry uses the synced `project.id` (`syncPrStatus`) or `connection.projectId` (the webhook). A PR-state entry names the states only, never the PR URL, title or merge author. Manual sync retains request actor/origin rest; poller/webhook retain SYSTEM/vcs and origin system. No entry in this feature sets `onBehalfOf`.

The five handlers are handlePullRequestOpened, handlePullRequestClosed (non-merged), handlePullRequestReadyForReview, handlePullRequestReopened and handlePullRequestConvertedToDraft. Preserve terminal checks, already-merged/not-found result mapping and ignored webhook responses. A record rejection rolls back the state; syncPrStatus counts that link skipped and continues (including failed 404-close writes); webhook throws into controller forget/retry behavior. Wire mockAuditRecorder into affected test providers/direct constructors and add required keys to ALL syncPrStatus calls without removing existing assertions (specific consumers in analysis). Use a local recorder stub that evaluates entriesOf for the zero-record unit case; global mockAuditRecorder intentionally does not.

**Scope** — In: non-merge PR-state audits, key forwarding and isolated 404 failure handling. Out: US-002 issue-import callbacks/shared helper creation; US-004 will change applyMergedPr and its actor/transition audits; US-005 owns derived-link audit behavior; US-006 wraps replay guard calls. Recording the update branches of `upsertTicketLink` and `upsertFleetPrLink`, a same-state webhook PR write, the poller's `VcsSyncLog` rows and cursor, the replay rows and a push's `code_commit` outbox rows is out of scope (the Bookkeeping table). Adding catalog keys (one per webhook event or per merge entry) is out of scope; each write records under its existing key and the summary names the event.

**Interface** — `VcsPrSyncService.syncPrStatus(project, connection, encryptionKey)` → `syncPrStatus(project, connection, encryptionKey, auditKey: VcsPrStateAuditKey)`. Import the upstream helper declarations unchanged:
```typescript
/** The key a PR-state write records: the entry point that saw the state. */
export type VcsPrStateAuditKey = 'vcs.sync.pr' | 'system.vcs.poll-issues' | 'system.vcs.webhook-intake';

/** `pr <before> -> <after>`; `before` is `none` for a link with no stored state. */
export function prStateSummary(before: string | null, after: string): string;
```

userStories.title: The PR merge step is audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make the shared PR merge step record its winning link write and eligible auto-transition as SYSTEM/vcs in their respective transactions.

**Motivation** — Every human route and every fleet writer now leaves an entry, but a ticket imported from a GitHub issue, a PR merge that moves a ticket to `VERIFY_FIX`, a VCS connection whose token was replaced and a ticket a CI pipeline opened leave none.

**Approach** — The merge step always records `system.vcs.pr-merge-transition`, as `SYSTEM/vcs`. `VcsPrSyncService` is the `@SystemWriter('system.vcs.pr-merge-transition')` class and `applyMergedPr` is "the one merge step" for every path (`vcs-pr-sync.service.ts:143`). It runs its writes inside `runAsSystemWriter(this, …)`, so a merge seen by the manual PR sync or by the fleet PR refresher (`SYSTEM/ticket-link`) is still recorded as `SYSTEM/vcs`. `runAsSystem` inherits the enclosing `correlationId`, so the entry still joins the request or tick that saw the merge. This follows audit-fleet-system's call "an entry under a `system.*` key always carries that component's actor".

A merge records two entries. One on the link (`pr <before> -> merged`), committed by the link write, and one on the ticket (`status: IN_PROGRESS -> VERIFY_FIX`), committed with the auto-transition. The FIX_REPORT comment and the `VCS_PR_MERGED` activity row are in the transition's transaction and covered by its entry, as audit-core's transition entries cover their comment.

`apps/api/src/vcs/vcs-pr-sync.service.ts` — applyMergedPr runs inside runAsSystemWriter(this, …), its link write inside audit.audited (recorded when 'updated'), and handleMergedPrAutoTransition runs applyMergedPrTransition inside audit.audited, recorded on the ticket; the conditional write, the IN_PROGRESS check and the logged-not-thrown transition failure are unchanged.

`projectId` is the row's project. A connection's, an imported ticket's, a fleet job's, the CI project's. A PR-state entry uses the synced `project.id` (`syncPrStatus`) or `connection.projectId` (the webhook). The merge step has only the link, so it uses `link.ticket?.projectId ?? null` (`TicketLinkData.ticket` is optional; every production caller loads it).

Contract:
| Write | Key | resourceType | resourceId | projectId | summary |
| PR merged: the link | `system.vcs.pr-merge-transition` | `ticket-link` | link id | `link.ticket?.projectId ?? null` | `prStateSummary(<before>, 'merged')` |
| PR merged: the auto-transition | `system.vcs.pr-merge-transition` | `ticket` | ticket id | `link.ticket?.projectId ?? null` | `status: IN_PROGRESS -> VERIFY_FIX` |

The merge step's two entries are always `SYSTEM/vcs`. No entry in this feature sets `onBehalfOf`. Do not include PR URL/title, merge author/SHA or comment contents in summaries. Two competing paths are gated by the existing conditional link update: only outcome updated records and attempts the transition. A non-IN_PROGRESS/missing ticket has only the link entry. Record failure on the link rolls it back and rejects to the caller's existing error path. Record failure on the transition rolls back ticket, FIX_REPORT and activity and is logged internally; the already committed link and entry stay merged. Keep separate audited calls; wrapping the entire merge in one transaction would violate AC9.

`FleetPrStateRefresher.apply` calls `applyMergedPr` for a merged PR (`fleet-pr-state.refresher.ts`); unchanged, it gets the merge entries through US-004. Keep its existing non-merge audit and knowledge event behavior; do not record an extra system.ticket-link.pr-refresh entry on a merge. Add the currentContext capture unit case to vcs-pr-sync.service.spec.ts; exercise direct SYSTEM/USER calls, the signed webhook and real app.get(FleetPrStateRefresher).refresh in the new real-AppModule integration spec.

**Scope** — In: shared merge link/transition auditing, SYSTEM/vcs boundary and concurrency/partial-failure behavior. Out: US-003 non-merge state handling; US-005 derived links and fleet terminal effects; US-006 intake replay attribution. Recording the merge step's FIX_REPORT comment or `VCS_PR_MERGED` activity row as entries of their own is out of scope; the transition's entry covers its transaction. An `onBehalfOf` on the merge step's entries when a user's PR sync or the fleet refresher saw the merge is out of scope; the shared `correlationId` joins them.

**Interface** — Preserve existing public signatures and outcome types:
```typescript
async applyMergedPr(link: TicketLinkData, prStatus: VcsPrStatus): Promise<PrStateWriteResult>
async handleMergedPrAutoTransition(link: TicketLinkData, prStatus: VcsPrStatus): Promise<void>
```
Use read-only `runAsSystemWriter(writer, fn)`, `AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf)` and upstream `prStateSummary(before: string | null, after: string): string`. Required recorder injection was added by US-003; no additional constructor change is needed.

userStories.title: Extracted links and fleet ticket effects are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Audit newly extracted branch/commit links and fleet terminal comments/PR links under their domain keys while preserving current actor and idempotent bookkeeping.

**Motivation** — Those are writes an outside system caused, and the Audit log is the only place that would show which integration made them and when.

**Approach** — Derived writes record under their domain key, as the current actor. A branch or commit link created by `VcsLinkExtractorService`, and the failure comment and PR link `FleetJobTicketEffects` writes, have no system key of their own: the extractor runs inside whichever entry point synced the PR, and the effects run after a job ends, as the runner (`RUNNER/<id>`), the sweeper (`SYSTEM/job`) or the ingest drain (`SYSTEM/ingest`). They record `ticket.link.add` and `comment.create`, the keys audit-core records for the same rows through the REST routes, and the entry's actor is whatever context is current.

Only a created link records. `upsertTicketLink` and `upsertFleetPrLink` each have an update branch for a link that already exists (the extractor refreshes `linkType` and `externalRef`; the fleet effect sets `jobId`). Those are bookkeeping. Both methods now return the created link's id, or `null` when the link existed, so the caller can record the new row.

The extractor's entries can land after `syncPrStatus` resolves. `syncPrStatus` starts `extractLinksFromPr` without awaiting it (`vcs-pr-sync.service.ts:111`) when the PR status has a `branchName` and the link has a ticket, so in the PR-sync route and the poller its `ticket.link.add` entries are written asynchronously, still under the caller's context. That is unchanged; tests of `syncPrStatus` stub a status without `branchName`.

`apps/api/src/vcs/vcs-link-extractor.service.ts` — injects AuditRecorder right after vcsRepo (before the optional vcsConfig) and runs each upsertTicketLink inside audit.audited, recording ticket.link.add when it returned a string (a stub resolving undefined records nothing); the provider calls and the ref matching are unchanged.
`apps/api/src/vcs/prisma-vcs.repository.ts` — upsertTicketLink returns the created link's id, or null when a link for (ticketId, url) existed and was updated; the writes are unchanged.
`apps/api/src/fleet/tickets/fleet-job-ticket.effects.ts` — injects AuditRecorder as the last constructor parameter, records comment.create in commentOnce after createSystemComment, and records ticket.link.add in linkPr when upsertFleetPrLink returned an id; the claim, the events and the per-ticket catch are unchanged.
`apps/api/src/fleet/tickets/prisma-fleet-tickets.repository.ts` — upsertFleetPrLink uses createManyAndReturn({ skipDuplicates }) and returns the created row's id, or null after updating the existing link's jobId.

Contract:
| Write | Key | resourceType | resourceId | projectId | summary |
| branch or commit link created by the extractor | `ticket.link.add` | `ticket-link` | the new link's id | the project | `on <KEY>-<number>` |
| fleet failure comment | `comment.create` | `comment` | comment id | the job's project | `on <ticket ref>` |
| fleet PR link created | `ticket.link.add` | `ticket-link` | the new link's id | the job's project | `on <ticket ref>` |

`<KEY>-<number>` and `<ticket ref>` are the ticket's ref, as audit-core's comment and link entries write it. The extractor's and the fleet effects' entries carry the current context's actor.
